identity: Unsigned PE32 managed GUI application presenting SaltwaterAquarium metadata; OriginalFilename DpdO.exe
confirmed_execution_chain: Main constructs TankForm. InitializeComponent reads the Virtual resource bitmap through CSAF.Run, walking pixels by column and collecting RGB bytes. The first 68,608 bytes are a managed PE loaded through AppDomain.CurrentDomain.Load(byte[]). Reflection and VB LateBinding invoke its entry method.

The first decoded assembly receives CVtd, cbn and the outer resource namespace. It crops the CVtd bitmap to 366 by 366, reads column-major BGRA bytes, obtains a four-byte payload length and decrypts the following bytes with XOR. The key loop wraps at the three-character string length, yielding the effective bytes 00 63 00; a second constant is 2d. This produces another managed assembly, loaded and invoked through reflection.

The second managed assembly uses .NET Reactor protection and an encrypted string table. Restricted arithmetic interpretation and reimplementation of its word cipher recover 100 strings. Its final resource payload is decrypted using the recovered SgGdwpfguqQGhb key and the observed XOR/subtraction byte transform.

The final resource is an importless native PE with an executable DOS stub and a self-decoding text section. Bounded Unicorn emulation with entirely synthetic Windows APIs confirms dynamic API resolution, virtual allocation, heap enumeration, marker-delimited code decryption and an attempted open of ntdll.dll. Emulation stops at the unmodeled NtCreateFile call.
capability_evidence_and_limits: Recovered managed strings and code contain Defender exclusion/policy manipulation, process-hollowing API resolution, and a CMSTP INF template spoofing a Microsoft VC++ update. Many configuration flags are zero; these are available routines/templates, not proof that each action executes in this configuration.
Rijndael helpers coexist with protected resources, but the observed string and payload paths use other transforms. Their co-occurrence does not establish AES resource decryption.

The native stage remains partially unresolved beyond its attempted ntdll reopen. No final malware-family attribution, command-and-control address, credential theft, or ntdll unhooking claim is established.

Sample code was not run on the host or loaded into a real CLR. Native analysis used an isolated CPU emulator with synthetic memory, exports and API responses; no sample-directed networking or filesystem operations were performed.
